newsitem.title: USA: Treasury's Summers says US must pay arrears.
newsitem.headline: Treasury's Summers says US must pay arrears.

text.p: Deputy Treasury Secretary Secretary Lawrence Summers said on Wednesday that it was "unconscionable" for the United States to owe arrears to international financial institutions.

Echoing comments made on Tuesday night by President Clinton in his State of the Union message, Summers told a bankers' group that the United States should quickly pay up the millions it owes in payments to international institutions like the World Bank.
"It is unconscionable for the wealthiest and most powerful country on earth to fail to meet its commitments," he said in remarks prepared for delivery to the Banker's Association for Foreign Trade.

The Clinton administration has been urging Congress for some time to pay the arrears. The United States is $234.5 million behind in payments to the World Bank's International Development Association, which lends to very poor countries.
Summers said the United States was "negotiating our commitment...downwards" but it was vital to support them financially in order to have a hand in their management.
He said it was "enormously in our national interest" to promote global propserity and a key means for doing so was by backing international financial institutions that foster growth.
Summers said that "a policy of engagement" through supporting multilateral bodies has helped the United States boost its exports by 7.2 percent a year since 1992.
He said 10 million jobs depended upon exports and urged the bankers' group to support Clinton administration efforts to negotiate agreements aimed at opening up world markets and expanding trade.
